result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.node_expansion()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the node expansion of a set of nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L51376-L51425){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.node_expansion(S) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Node expansion](/assets/graphs/node-expansion.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same graph and set S. Every neighbor of a member counts, members included: A, B and C are adjacent to each other, and D and E lie across the cut, all five in accent. Five neighbors over three members gives node expansion 5 / 3 = 1.667." width="100%"} The number of nodes adjacent to the set divided by the size of the set, as in NetworkX's `node_expansion()`. Note that this counts *every* neighbor of a member, including other members; for neighbors outside the set only (the vertex expansion of expander-graph theory), use `boundary_expansion()`. On a directed graph, neighbors are nodes the set points to. Self-loops are ignored (NetworkX counts a node with a self-loop as its own neighbor), and `S=` is treated as a set, so repeated nodes count once. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [S]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node expansion. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `S=` is empty or a node does not exist. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The triangle A, B, C has four distinct neighbors, counting its own members: A, B and C (each adjacent to the others) plus D. Only D lies outside it: ::: {#5bf5c8d3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) ) graph.node_expansion(["A", "B", "C"]), graph.boundary_expansion(["A", "B", "C"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (1.3333333333333333, 0.3333333333333333) ``` ::: :::
